To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
calponin and caldemon levels are increased in cerebral microvessels during sustained contractility following TBI.
Cp and Cd expressions in cerebral microvessels are upregulated following TBI, and that the proteins compartmentalize to specific cellular domains.
Cp and Cd expressions are upregulated in cerebral SM and En following TBI.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that regulate the contractility of microvessels in the brain.
the identification and characterization of Cp and Cd as potential markers of cerebral microvessel contractility following traumatic brain injury.
the identification of Cp and Cd as novel markers of reacting microvessles in the injured brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results suggest a role for these proteins during microvascular contraction following TBI.
calponin (Cpn) and caldesmom (Cdm) levels increase while compartmenting to specific subcellualr domains.
Cp and Cd are actin-binding cytoskeletal proteins that regulate blood vessel tone and are involved in the pathophysiology of TBI-induced cerebral hypoperfusion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the upregulation of Cp and Cd, as well as their compartmentalization to specific domains, may underlie the sustained contraction observed in reacting microvasculature following traumatic brain injury (TIBI).
the expression and localization of Cp and Cd are altered in microvessels in response to TBI, which may play a role in the sustained contractility observed in reacting blood vessels.
Cp and Cd upregulation in microvessels is a temporal event, which may be involved in the pathophysiology of cerebral hypoperfusion after TBI.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Cp and Cd are expressed in cerebral microvessels during TBI and their expressions are temporally associated to the state of contractility in reacting vessels.
calponin and caldemon, two actin-binding proteins that regulate smooth muscle contractility, are up-regulated after traumatic brain injury.
Cp and Cd are involved in the regulation and compartmentalization of the actin cytoskeleton and the contractile apparatus of both SM and En.
